grade_rationale.text: Máchal records the Domovoy for Russians, and his house-spirit under other names for the Little Russians (Ukrainians) and in a rite of the White Russians.
Ralston records the Domovoy in several Russian governments, in White-Russia as the house snake, in Poland and in Lusatia.
Máchal and Ralston independently describe a hairy old man who guards the household, in different wording and detail.
Ralston's 28 January kasha passage cites Afanasyev ('says Afanasief'), so that clause is counted once with Afanasyev, not as independent.
Afanasyev gives the house-spirit's names among the Belarusians and in Poland.
